stories.title: Apple Music 7.0 brings Liquid Glass to Android
stories.summary: Apple Music for Android now uses the translucent, floating Liquid Glass look and jumps its version number to match iOS 27. The bottom bar floats above content and the app runs edge to edge. Apple has not published release notes confirming every change.

stories.title: Apple's first touchscreen MacBook Pro gets bigger buttons when you reach for them
stories.summary: The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is Apple's first Mac with a touch display. Window controls grow when tapped, trackpad gestures work on the screen itself, and Spotlight can be opened from the Dynamic Island, as on iOS 27.

stories.title: Gemini's sparkling overlay spreads beyond Pixel phones
stories.summary: Google is rolling out a redesigned Gemini overlay to Android phones through the Google app, starting October 29. Glowing particles and coloured dots now surround the Ask Gemini box as it opens, a look previously limited to Pixel 11 devices.

stories.title: Clio demos legal software like an Apple keynote
stories.summary: At ClioCon, CEO Jack Newton walked more than 3,000 attendees through a full legal matter in seven minutes. An AI voice agent takes the first call, then AI helps lawyers with research, drafting, filing and billing, and finally asks the client for a review.

stories.title: A week with the iPhone Duo, two phones and one change of heart
stories.summary: A TechCrunch reporter took Apple's new iPhone Duo on a five-day vacation and kept threatening to switch back, citing broken apps, unfamiliar gestures, the return of Touch ID and camera worries. By the end of the trip she did not want to go back.

stories.title: CD Projekt Red gets a creator platform with no tiers
stories.summary: 180heartbeats and Jung v Matt designed the UX and UI for CD Projekt Red's Creators and Ambassadors Program, aimed at streamers, cosplayers and artists inspired by The Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077. Members get assets, free games and rewards, and nobody is sorted into ranks.

stories.title: Cuberto designs a mobile bank that avoids looking like a spreadsheet
stories.summary: Cuberto built the UI and UX for Wickret, a zero-fee mobile bank applying for a national charter with AI-assisted savings. The system uses Montserrat type grids, colour-blocked wallet cards and a cobalt wordmark whose W splits into a V and a slash.

stories.title: Edge's Reading Mode becomes an accidental ad blocker
stories.summary: A Windows Central writer says some pages now slip past his ad blockers on Android, so he leans on Microsoft Edge's Reading Mode instead. The accessibility feature strips pages back to the text, which turns out to be most of what he wanted.

stories.title: Khaleeji Bank redesigns its mobile app
stories.summary: Khaleeji Bank has launched a redesigned mobile app with a 6.25% investment return and family banking features, according to an FF News headline. Only the headline was available to us, so details of the new interface are not yet known.

stories.title: Windows Security gets a modernised UX for Insiders
stories.summary: Neowin reports that Windows Security is getting a major update for Windows Insiders with a modernised user experience. The full article was blocked to us and only the headline was available, so the specific interface changes are not described here.

stories.title: Pentagram builds a Thai restaurant identity around just for fun
stories.summary: Pentagram's branding for LenLen, a Manhattan Thai shophouse whose name means just for fun in Thai, pairs an inflated bubble typeface with a quick marker hand and a tiger-cat. The bubble letters run posters and signage while the marker writes the menu.

stories.title: Mother Design held a seance to rebrand a psychic platform
stories.summary: For psychic services platform Purple Garden, Mother Design worked with a holistic practitioner and ran seances and chakra readings as part of the process. Jo Tulej explains how the experiments under the studio's Wild Card initiative shaped the new identity.

stories.title: Vercel's Geist specimen site lets you stress-test the type
stories.summary: Vercel has built an interactive specimen site for its Geist typeface family that works like a testing lab. Engineers and typographers can try weight transitions, check glyph anchors and examine optical balance on screen, in a layout that leans on Swiss typography.

stories.title: A deodorant brand borrows from West End theatre marquees
stories.summary: London studio Two Times Elliott designed AKT London's identity around theatre canopy boards and script directions. The plastic-free deodorant balm comes in aluminium tubes, and each scent carries a scene code such as SC.02 EXT. AFTER THUNDER.

stories.title: Underline Studio packs 75 years of Canadian advertising into one book
stories.summary: Toronto's Underline Studio designed Archive/Recollection for the Advertising and Design Club of Canada's 75th anniversary. The clothbound book draws on ADCC annuals from 1949 to 2024 and arrives in a grey slipcase stamped with a gold foil 75.

stories.title: The best book covers of October include one by a former indie musician
stories.summary: The Rumpus picks 12 October covers, led by Jared Bartman's design for Rebecca Perry's May We Feed the King. Bartman spent a decade as an indie musician, took a UX bootcamp around 2020 and found he preferred designing book covers.

stories.title: Smashing Magazine's November wallpapers are here
stories.summary: Smashing Magazine's monthly wallpaper collection, a tradition running for more than 15 years, brings free November desktop backgrounds from artists and designers around the world. Each comes in several screen resolutions, with the stated aim of brightening a gray month.

stories.title: Bath Township police retire a 40-year-old eagle logo
stories.summary: Bath Township's dispatch and police department has its first visual rebrand in 40 years, replacing a bald eagle holding an olive branch and arrows. The department's communications team designed the new logo in-house for updated uniforms, starting with a darker patch.

stories.title: Dolmio brings back its puppet family after ten years
stories.summary: For its 40th anniversary, Dolmio has revived the puppet family from its 2000s adverts after a ten-year break. Elmwood London's Kyle Whybrow tells Creative Bloq that nostalgia is a double-edged sword and audiences are hungry for tactile, human-led design.

stories.title: Rockstar art-directed 600,000 animations for GTA 6 passers-by
stories.summary: Rockstar Games says it art-directed 600,000 animations so that background characters in Grand Theft Auto 6 feel like real people, according to an Edge cover feature reported by Creative Bloq. Non-player characters are usually treated as visual wallpaper.

stories.title: Czech graphic design gets a show in Brussels
stories.summary: Identita, a show on Czech graphic design, runs at Design Museum Brussels until March 7, 2027. Across 400 square metres it gathers Prague metro signs, film posters, books and typefaces, tracing Czech visual identity from the search for a national style to the changes after 1989.

stories.title: Figma says AI made drafts fast and quality slow
stories.summary: Figma's Asia-Pacific sales vice president Rene Lo told The Seoul Economic Daily that AI makes first drafts easy but shippable quality now takes far more effort. With AI agents handling code, she said, design polish is becoming the thing that sets products apart.

stories.title: Adobe Firefly now works with more than 10 partner AI models
stories.summary: Adobe has expanded Firefly to support over 10 third-party AI models for image and video creation, including models commonly used in India, Oneindia reports. The idea is that creative professionals can switch between models without leaving the tool.

stories.title: Hebrew University paper says AI is not killing art
stories.summary: A new paper from Prof. Amit Zoran of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem argues that generative AI is not making human artists obsolete. It strips away technical barriers, he says, and the real question is whether the process of making something has value the finished piece cannot capture.

stories.title: A production designer argues AI is not the end of practical craft
stories.summary: Christopher Glass, an ADG Award-winning production designer with over 20 years in film, tells Creative Bloq that there is still room for tactile, practical design. His advice to newcomers worried about AI is to use their tools against them.

stories.title: A designer returns from DesignThinkers with curiosity as the takeaway
stories.summary: Writing for PRINT, a Canadian designer working in New York recalls returning to Toronto for the Registered Graphic Designers' DesignThinkers conference on October 20 and 21. In the age of AI, she argues, curiosity is the most useful creative tool designers have.

stories.title: Canva's first Dutch campaign has bad designs singing
stories.summary: DEPT's first work for Canva in the Netherlands rewrites the Dutch song Ik wou dat ik jou was for a cast of singing design disasters. A clashing wedding card, a cringe social post and a clip-art light bulb all long to be better designs.

stories.title: Canva launches Brush as a survey puts designer AI use at 79.7%
stories.summary: Canva has released Brush, its first vision-language model, which reads layouts, layers and design intent to edit with users. A report cited by The Kobeissi Letter says 79.7% of designers now use AI in at least one stage of their work.

stories.title: Fast Company asks whether Canva's newest AI feature can end design slop
stories.summary: Fast Company asks whether Canva's newest AI feature could end graphic design slop. The article was blocked to us and only the headline was available, so we cannot say which feature it covers or what answer it reaches.

stories.title: The people using AI should set its strategy, a researcher argues
stories.summary: A UX Collective piece argues that practitioners, who know what good output looks like, should own AI decisions while operations handles the plumbing. Its opening scene has a researcher checking an AI synthesis against her own notes. Only part of the article was available.

stories.title: Figma Weave turns AI generation into reusable workflows
stories.summary: Figma Weave strings AI generation and editing tools into connected node workflows that teams can branch, refine and repeat. A finished workflow can be packaged as a Weave tool so colleagues can run it without touching the nodes underneath.

stories.title: Adobe MAX 2026 heads back to Miami Beach
stories.summary: Adobe MAX runs November 10 to 12 at the Miami Beach Convention Center, with an online option. The opening keynote is set for two hours on November 10, shorter than last year's three-hour opener, and Sneaks will again preview experimental tools.

stories.title: Text-to-cad lets coding agents design physical products
stories.summary: Text-to-cad is a free, open-source plugin that lets AI agents generate 3D models as STEP, GLB, STL or 3MF files. It runs design for manufacturing checks, makes engineering drawings and connects to 3D printing, sheet metal and CNC services.

stories.title: How to make your own Inktober brushes in Procreate
stories.summary: Creative Bloq artist Phoebe Shore has a short video tutorial on making spooky ink brushes in Procreate. You will need an iPad, since Procreate does not run on Android tablets or Windows PCs. The writer recommends brush number 3 for splatters.

stories.title: Webflow shows how to build a filterable property listing feed
stories.summary: A Webflow tutorial builds a small Next.js app on Webflow Cloud that reads property listings from the CMS and filters them by city and bedrooms on the server. The API token stays out of the browser, and the same endpoint can feed partner sites.

stories.title: Webflow explains moving a Squarespace blog without breaking links
stories.summary: Webflow's guide to moving Squarespace posts into its CMS says to try the CSV import first. For larger archives it builds a small Webflow Cloud importer that keeps every slug and original publish date and shows which record failed.

stories.title: Lenovo's Googlebook 15 has a good screen and a hard sell
stories.summary: Summarising PCWorld's review, NeoTeo says the Lenovo Googlebook 15 pairs a strong 15.3-inch OLED touchscreen with an uncomfortable keyboard, uneven software responsiveness and short battery life. The reviewer concluded the experience did not justify the US price.

stories.title: Figma stock may move 13% on its November 4 results
stories.summary: Investing.com reports that Figma shares may move 13% around its earnings release on November 4. Only the headline was available to us, so we cannot say which direction analysts expect or what is driving the estimate.

stories.title: NID symposium traces drawing from chalk to stylus
stories.summary: Drawing Dialogues 2026 at NID's Gandhinagar campus brought experts together to discuss drawing as the most basic form of design. Prof Kaushik Chakraborty said work in engineering, architecture, fashion and automobile design often starts with pencil and paper.

stories.title: Indian designers push paper and fabric lights past the lampshade
stories.summary: Designers are reworking paper and fabric lighting through hand processes, unusual forms and texture, the Times of India reports. Amrita Nambiar, founder of Olie, says these familiar materials offer enormous possibilities when transformed through new techniques.

stories.title: The Hindu picks handcrafted Diwali gifts from Indian studios
stories.summary: The Hindu's Diwali gift guide rounds up objects from studios across India. Picks include Kaunteya's marble inlay cheese platter from Indore with Phad wedding motifs at Rs 11,580, and Khanoom's hand-painted Jaipur platters finished with 24-carat gold lustre.

stories.title: Neytt turns Indian landmarks into woven wall art
stories.summary: Kerala design house Neytt, which once made a carpet for the Met Gala, has an 1854 Collection of woven artworks in sisal, wool and bamboo silk. Inspired by postage stamps, they depict the Qutub Minar, Gateway of India and Kochi's backwaters. Much of the article is behind a paywall.

stories.title: Karishma Shahani Khan opens her process to the public in Mumbai
stories.summary: Pune designer Karishma Shahani Khan's free showcase TARA runs at 47-A in Khotachiwadi until November 8. It explains her label Ka-Sha and its sister initiative Heart to Haat, which turns production waste into fabric flowers, home textiles, garments and footwear.

stories.title: Mumbai artist Rouble Nagi wins the $1 million Global Teacher Prize
stories.summary: Rouble Nagi, who has turned neglected walls in more than 100 underserved communities into educational murals, has won the GEMS Education Global Teacher Prize 2026. She was chosen from over 5,000 nominations across 139 countries, the Times of India reports.

stories.title: Bengaluru studio launches rhythm game SURI on PS5
stories.summary: Tathvamasi Studios has released SURI: The Seventh Note on PlayStation 5 and PC, the first major release from Sony's PlayStation India Hero Project. Its own haptics engine turns live instrument recordings into DualSense feedback within a 480-millisecond beat window.

stories.title: Mumbai's Gamebee Studio builds Indian games for the world
stories.summary: India has 555 million gamers, yet its ten top-grossing games are global franchises, Outlook reports. Mumbai's Gamebee Studio, founded in 2019 without outside funding, has more than 70 games on TV, mobile and PC and reports over 40 million downloads.

stories.title: KRAFTON India picks eight indie studios for its fourth PitchFest
stories.summary: KRAFTON India's Gaming Incubator held its fourth PitchFest at the India Game Developer Conference in Chennai on October 30. Eight studios chosen from over 300 applications, including Kalp and Tandoori Pixels, had ten minutes each before a 12-member jury.

stories.title: Studio Tara makes fine jewellery that does not take itself seriously
stories.summary: Chennai designer Bharathi Ramamurthy has run bespoke atelier Studio Tara for 26 years, building pieces around untreated coloured gems such as peridot, garnet and tanzanite. She calls her ethos bold but quiet and says real luxury shows in restraint.

stories.title: Instamart puts a man in a chandelier for Diwali
stories.summary: Instamart's in-house team made a Diwali film in which a husband returns from a late party wearing a crystal chandelier as an outfit, apparently on low battery. The ad uses the couple's matter-of-fact conversation to sell its festive decor range.

stories.title: Delhi government school students take a horror game to Seoul
stories.summary: Four students from Dr BR Ambedkar School of Specialised Excellence in Lajpat Nagar presented a 3D horror game built in Unity at the Better Ground gaming showcase in Seoul. The team, called Immortals, represented India at the event.

stories.title: Tuticorin Alkali Chemicals puts its logo in a carbon bond
stories.summary: Soda ash maker Tuticorin Alkali Chemicals and Fertilisers has a new identity as it looks beyond its traditional markets. The logo places the letters TFL inside a hexagon inspired by carbon bonds, and green stays as the main brand colour.

stories.title: Sebastian Thrun's Dulo raises $130 million to design hardware with AI
stories.summary: Dulo, co-founded this year by Sebastian Thrun and Adrian Aoun, has raised a $130 million seed round to build what it calls Engineering Superintelligence for hardware design. Backers include Marc Benioff, John Doerr and Eric Schmidt, according to The Information.

stories.title: Phinity Labs raises $5.2 million for AI that designs chips from prompts
stories.summary: Phinity Labs, led by Sonya Jin and Aadi Nashikkar, has raised a $5.2 million seed round led by Uncork Capital to build AI agents that design computer chips from text prompts. Jeff Dean is among the angel investors.

stories.title: Indian startups raised about $115 million last week
stories.summary: Indian startups raised about $115 million across 28 deals from October 26 to 31, according to Entrackr. AI companies Simplismart and Live2.ai took around $14 million each, with Bengaluru's Simplismart closing a Series B led by Dallas Venture Capital.

stories.title: Three startups took 90% of a week's funding
stories.summary: Of nearly $43 million raised across seven rounds tracked by CIOL from October 26 to 30, Cent, Live2.ai and Matiks took roughly 90%. The other four startups shared about $4.1 million, and Inkle expanded in the US through an acquisition.

stories.title: YK-Robotics raises a seed round to program factory robots in plain words
stories.summary: YK-Robotics has raised a one million euro seed round for software that lets factories program robots using plain language, according to a Dealroom headline. The full article was blocked, so only the headline was available to us.

stories.title: Lagos designer says design shapes how families and offices work
stories.summary: Osaru Alile-Abraham, founder of Design House, unveiled an open house showcase and documentary for Design Week Lagos 2026. She said designing spaces showed her how physical surroundings shape family relationships, and that good workplaces can lift productivity.

stories.title: A Hanoi graphic designer swapped her desk for a blowtorch
stories.summary: After four years in graphic design, Nguyen Thu Ha, born in 2000, now makes glass flowers in Hanoi over flames reaching 1,600 degrees Celsius. She found the craft through a video of a glass lotus and sells pieces for up to $40.

stories.title: Plus Collaboratives on how Singapore design changed
stories.summary: Mervin Tan and Cheryl Sim of Singapore studio Plus Collaboratives tell Branding in Asia how local design moved from top-down nation-building work to a softer approach that seeks to persuade. They say clients are now more willing to take risks on bolder choices.

stories.title: Type Directors Club names six new advisory board members
stories.summary: The Type Directors Club has added Gary Fogelson, Beatriz Lozano, Monika Marek-Lucka, Audrie Poole, Nina Stossinger and Rich Tu to its advisory board for two-year terms. Lozano, now in Mexico City, wants to support young designers across borders and languages.

stories.title: EDGE Awards 2027 opens for entries
stories.summary: The EDGE Awards 2027 are taking entries for innovation in product design and function across 16 categories. Winners are chosen by readers of titles including Machine Design, Electronic Design and Automation World. Only a short announcement was available.

stories.title: Seoul says pairing small firms with designers opened new markets
stories.summary: A Chosun Ilbo report says a Seoul design programme backing small and medium businesses drove market growth with 2.79 billion won of support and 74 intellectual property rights. Only the headline and summary line were available, so programme details are not covered here.
